source.title: Small Data, Big Decisions: Model Selection in the Small-Data Regime
source.authors: J. Bornschein; Francesco Visin; Simon Osindero

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplement are present; minor text-extraction artifacts do not obscure the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly sweeps neural-network size and training-set size and reports generalization outcomes, but uses a different experimental focus and principally reports calibrated cross-entropy rather than the original studies’ test-error curves.
record.gate_note: The paper varies model size, training-set size, and training time and reports evaluation results. Results cited from prior work are not recorded. Values visible only in plots are marked figure only; the paper does not provide extractable numerical values for these curves in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps model width/channels at several training-set sizes (Fig. 3, 4, supplement). It states it never quite sees the double-descent spike, with artifacts only for the CIFAR10 MLP. This bears directly on V1 by a different method (temperature-calibrated cross-entropy, no label noise). Learning curves (Fig. 1) bear weakly on V2. The data-size sweeps cannot show V3 because the compared models were deliberately chosen beyond their interpolation threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that temperature calibration makes generalization cross-entropy well behaved, which enables MDL estimates. They add that small-data training can improve the model-selection signal (SNR) while saving compute. The absence of a spike is a side observation, not a main conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps training-set size extensively and includes model-size and learning-curve experiments; its main analysis is model ranking and calibrated generalization cross-entropy, rather than reproducing the original double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports experiments with different optimizers and architectures, and says some choices affect performance-over-data-size curves. It reports that model rankings did not cross outside uncertainty bands in its tested variations.

fits_no_version.finding: Temperature calibration removes the overfitting signature of held-out cross-entropy. Calibrated cross-entropy tracks error rate closely.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-based overfitting/double-descent signatures in cross-entropy are largely overconfidence and vanish after temperature calibration.

fits_no_version.finding: Model size needed for near-optimal performance appears independent of training-set size (about 384 channels for ResNet-101 at both 10k and 1.2M samples).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal model size for overparameterized nets does not shrink with less data.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119 (2020)
record.problems: Most relevant curves provide no numerical values in the supplied text and must be read from figures. The size-sweep evidence chiefly reports evaluation cross-entropy rather than direct test-error values, and the paper does not numerically locate an interpolation threshold or a peak.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant model-by-condition curves were extracted from the supplementary size-scaling plots; the main-text size-sweep results and the separate dataset-size curves for the model comparisons are represented above.

untested.parts: No label-noise conditions. No raw test-error size sweep in the main text (calibrated cross-entropy only). No located interpolation peak.
No explicit epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curve or peak location.
No curves for models near the interpolation threshold as sample size varies. Sample-wise non-monotonicity is not examined.
No label noise, regularization tuning, or multiple-descent tests. Temperature calibration is not a version-6 regularizer test.

missing.what: Model-size sweeps for MLP on MNIST, EMNIST and CIFAR10, and for ResNet-20 on CIFAR10, across data sizes. The authors say spike artifacts were 'usually not recognizable' outside the CIFAR10 MLP. rows_left_out mentions these sweeps, but they bear on V1 and should be rows.
missing.locator: Supplement, Scaling the Model Size; Section 4.2

record.verdict_notes: The study is not one of the originals. The double-descent evidence is secondary to the paper's ranking hypothesis. All V1/V2 evidence is figure-only plus verbal statements, and uses calibrated cross-entropy. The authors claim error-rate results would agree. The absence of label noise and the use of calibration and learning-rate tuning may explain the missing peak. The V1 'challenges' label should therefore be read as applying only to clean-label, calibrated settings.

versions.untested_parts: No numeric peak location or direct test-error values are provided for the size sweeps; most reported size-sweep curves use calibrated evaluation cross-entropy.
The paper does not report a complete fall-rise-fall test-error curve over epochs or locate a peak relative to interpolation.
The supplied text does not state that increasing sample size raises test error near an interpolation threshold, nor identify such a threshold on the sample-size curves.
The paper does not test double descent across general model classes past interpolation; it studies neural-network architectures and does not establish the proposed general curve.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested as predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study does not test label-noise or variance as a peak mechanism, multiple/triple descent, or disappearance of peaks under optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not re-count complexity using effective parameters or test whether this turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Tracked learning curves and generalization performance during training.
rows.value: figure only; the text reports a small degradation around the point where the rapid decrease in training error tapers off
rows.note: The text says the error rate tends to flatline rather than degrade significantly in the overfitting cases; it also reports a small generalization degradation around a training-progress transition. It does not describe a full fall-rise-fall epoch-wise curve.
rows.check: The value mixes two curves. Uncalibrated cross-entropy rises monotonically (overfitting, no second descent). The error rate flatlines. A small degradation near the training-error taper can be reduced with bigger models. Only a weak, partial echo of an epoch-wise bump; no fall-rise-fall is described.
